title: Integrated Controls, Biological Options and Outcome Review

content.overview: Integrated plant-health management combines prevention and compatible controls instead of relying on one reactive treatment. For cannabis, legal product availability varies by jurisdiction, so the curriculum emphasizes control categories, evidence and records rather than universal pesticide instructions.

vocabulary.definition: A production practice changed to make pest or disease establishment less favorable.
Use of living organisms or their ecological interactions to suppress a pest or pathogen.
A documented comparison of expected and observed outcomes after an intervention.

sections.title: Prevention has multiple layers
sections.body: Clean stock, sanitation, quarantine, environmental management and rapid removal of confirmed sources can reduce opportunities for pathogens to reproduce and spread.

sections.title: Biological and biorational tools are context dependent
sections.body: Published cannabis disease-management reviews describe promising biological and reduced-risk options while also noting that product claims are not always supported by replicated third-party data. Legal authorization must be checked separately.

sections.title: Every intervention needs an outcome measure
sections.body: Repeat scouting after a control action and compare incidence, severity and new spread with the baseline. Without follow-up, efficacy remains assumed rather than measured.

workedExamples: If sanitation improves but new cases continue along a humidity gradient, environmental correction may be part of the integrated response.
A biological product used without baseline scouting cannot be credited for improvement merely because symptoms later decline.
commonMistakes: Using one control repeatedly without checking efficacy.
Assuming a product is legal because it is sold online.
content.practicalApplication: Write an IPM action record containing diagnosis confidence, affected area, prevention steps, legal/product verification where relevant, selected controls, application responsibility, follow-up date and outcome metric.
content.summary: Integrated management is a documented sequence of prevention, diagnosis, compatible controls and measured follow-up.
